content: 1. Pharmacodynamic Synergism: When two drugs are co-administered, they may enhance each other's photosensitizing effects. It is recommended to avoid or use alternative drugs in such cases. 2. Metolazone and Trimethoprim: These drugs have an unspecified interaction mechanism with minor significance. Close monitoring is advised. 3. Metolazone and Sulfamethoxazole: Metolazone may increase sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 4. Metronidazole and Sulfamethoxazole: Metronidazole can increase sulfamethoxazole levels by reducing its metabolism via hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Miconazole Vaginal and Sulfamethoxazole: Miconazole may increase sulfamethoxazole levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 6. Trimethoprim and Microbiota Oral: Trimethoprim reduces the efficacy of microbiota oral products due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Complete antibiotic regimens 2-4 days before initiating microbiota oral therapy. 7. Sulfamethoxazole and Midodrine: Sulfamethoxazole increases midodrine levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 8. Trimethoprim and Midodrine: Midodrine increases trimethoprim levels through the same renal clearance competition. Monitor closely. 9. Mineral Oil and Sulfamethoxazole: Mineral oil decreases sulfamethoxazole levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 10. Mipomersen and Sulfamethoxazole: Both drugs may increase each other's toxicity by elevating hepatic enzymes. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely. 11. Mitotane and Trimethoprim: Mitotane decreases trimethoprim levels by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP3A4. Monitor closely and adjust dosages as needed. 12. Trimethoprim and Moexipril: Both drugs increase serum potassium levels, potentially causing hyperkalemia, especially in high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. Monitor potassium levels closely. 13. Sulfamethoxazole and Moxifloxacin: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 14. Sulfamethoxazole and Nateglinide: Sulfamethoxazole increases nateglinide levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism and plasma protein binding competition. Monitor closely. 15. Sulfamethoxazole and Nilotinib: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Nilotinib also increases sulfamethoxazole levels via CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitor closely. 16. Nitazoxanide and Sulfamethoxazole: These drugs may increase each other's levels through plasma protein binding competition. The clinical significance is unknown. 17. Nitisinone and Trimethoprim: Nitisinone increases trimethoprim levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9. Use caution and monitor closely, especially with drugs that have a narrow therapeutic index. 18. Nortriptyline and Sulfamethoxazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole decreases nortriptyline levels through an unspecified mechanism. Monitor closely. 19. Octreotide and Trimethoprim: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 20. Sulfamethoxazole and Ofloxacin: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole increases ofloxacin levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Monitor closely. 21. Trimethoprim and Olmesartan: Both drugs increase serum potassium levels, potentially causing hyperkalemia. Monitor potassium levels closely. 22. Sulfamethoxazole and Ospemifene: Sulfamethoxazole increases ospemifene levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism and plasma protein binding competition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 23. Trimethoprim and Paclitaxel: Trimethoprim increases paclitaxel levels by inhibiting CYP2C8 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust paclitaxel dosage if needed. 24. Sulfamethoxazole and Paliperidone: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Trimethoprim and Pantothenic Acid: Trimethoprim decreases pantothenic acid levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 26. Sulfamethoxazole and Parecoxib: Sulfamethoxazole increases parecoxib levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Trimethoprim and Paroxetine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 28.
